title: Solar eclipse
summary: Shoot the sun safely through a solar filter.

media.alt: Total solar eclipse: a black disc ringed by the white corona

blocks.text: **Eyes and sensor first.** Never look at the sun, or through the viewfinder, without certified eclipse glasses (**ISO 12312-2**). Put a proper **white-light solar filter** over the front of the lens. An ordinary ND filter is not safe.

blocks.alt: Eclipse sequence: filter on for partial phases, off only during totality
blocks.caption: The filter only comes off during totality, and only if you're inside the path of totality.

steps: Check the eclipse's path and times at timeanddate.com. The next total eclipse near Europe is **2 August 2027** (southern Spain, North Africa).
Practise on an ordinary sunny day with the filter: framing, focus and exposure all carry over.
Filter on. Manual mode, ISO 100, f/8, 1/1000 s. Focus manually on the sun's edge or a sunspot.
Partial phases: shoot every few minutes. Check the histogram, not the screen, for exposure.
At totality only: take the filter off and bracket from 1/1000 s to 1 s to catch inner and outer corona.
Filter back on the moment the first bright bead of sun appears.

items: Partial-only eclipse where you are? The filter stays on the whole time.
Totality lasts minutes. Bracket with auto exposure bracketing and spend the rest of the time watching.
Set a phone alarm for the end of totality so you don't forget the filter.
